written: 2026-11-21T12:35Z, after the exact-resolution run was stopped (record fixpoint:stopped) and before harness/fixladder.py existed; Fix.coarse_front_within was proved first
why: At exact resolution the front doubled every round and no fixed point was in reach. Chris's own rule for this project is that resolution is fixed at its coarsest grain but parametric. So the stop is certified one resolution at a time.
resolution: objective i is read in steps of r_i (floor). Level k uses r = max(1, R0 >> k) with R0 = [work 64, ban_hits 32, topic_misses 32, end_misses 32, loops 32, drift 1024 logits]. Level 10 is r = 1 everywhere, the exact front. R0 was set from the ranges of PR 4's final front (work 1-106, ban 0-48, topic 240, end 0-223, loops 0-280, drift 0-2723) before any run at these resolutions.
procedure: level 0: PR 4's proposal rule (phase A) and then unit-neighbourhood closure (phase B), both on the archive of coarsened vectors. Each later level: rebuild the archive of all evaluated points at the new resolution, then phase B to closure. Every evaluation is kept across levels. Lean `prlm front` over the coarsened vectors must equal the archive after every round.
certificate: a level counts as certified when its phase B has nothing to evaluate. Then Fix.closed_local_opt holds for the coarsened objectives, and by Fix.coarse_front_within anything that exactly dominates a front point does so by less than r_i in every objective
stop: level 10 certified, or 200,000 DEV evaluations in total (the finest certified level is then the result)
test_and_controls: the finest certified front is scored on TEST (exact objectives) against the round-0 front and PR 4's final front, both ways. Random: the same number of DEV evaluations at uniform random levels (seed 1), coarsened at the finest certified resolution, front scored on TEST both ways. GAMED: the same ladder on TEST up to the same level. Lean replay on all 1,440 steps of every point of the finest certified front if it has at most 600 points, otherwise of every point of the finest certified front with at most 600 points
verdict_rule: the result is the finest certified level, stated with its resolution; a fixed point at exact resolution is claimed only if level 10 is certified
